agent.name: Organizational Adoption of Emerging Technologies Agent
agent.specialty: SubAgent 6 - organizational readiness, prioritized gaps and sustainable operating ownership

analytical_question: Can this organization absorb, govern and sustain one reporting team’s proposed human-reviewed chart-to-source workflow? Separate task fit from readiness, identify the most consequential organizational gap and prioritized owners/actions, and ask for essential missing evidence.
general_et_finding: Organizational adoption is a socio-technical capacity question: accountable leadership, competent people, workable processes, authorized data/infrastructure, resources, governance, change acceptance and operating ownership must support the stated scope. Low readiness does not establish low technology maturity; favorable organizational conditions do not establish model capability or value. S1/S2 supply voluntary risk-management guidance, not a readiness score or implementation approval.
application_finding: Human-supervised read-only chart-to-source review is a plausible task-technology fit if sources, periods and denominators can be checked and corrections remain subject to human approval. Representative technical reliability and incremental value over manual/deterministic review remain unproved in every profile. An organizational improvement cannot change that application evidence or authorize autonomous publication. Feasibility PoC, comparative value and sustainable operation require separate evidence.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: All organizational profiles are fictional case premises, not actual company evidence or permissions.
No current vendor capability, negotiated price, regulation-specific conclusion, model reliability or local ROI is established.
Current same-assistant qualitative examples are not isolated independent inference runs or a deployed chart pilot.
Unknown is neither a passed check nor evidence of absence; case-supported organizational conditions do not prove strategic value.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Confidence is high in the conditional logic and the distinction between stated gap and unknown, but limited by fictional/incomplete organizational evidence and unproved application performance. No measured reliability or real organization certification is asserted.
value_opportunity_implication: A well-resourced source-linked review workflow might be useful, but its quality-adjusted value versus adequate manual/deterministic review remains a separate unproved proposition. Protected checking/support effort must be budgeted rather than hidden.
risk_governance_implication: No unapproved data/model route or autonomous publication. Require an accountable owner, competent human review, stop/incident/rollback and change reassessment for the actual scope. This readiness advice is not legal certification or release authority. Human decision-makers retain the final adoption/release judgment.
recommendation_management_implication: LIMITED_LEARNING_ONLY — fictional L1 supports only public/synthetic isolated feasibility learning, eight total analyst-hours over two weeks with its stipulated owner, reviewer, stop controls and logs. No internal data, routine work or autonomous publication is approved. Use the PoC to examine source-linked behavior and the human workflow; preserve failures and full effort. Routine readiness remains unestablished until recurrent staffing, ownership, operating controls/funding and independent application qualification are evidenced. Actual humans must authorize the activity.
change_monitoring_triggers: Documented scope-specific permission and accountable ownership can remove a blocker; loss of either reverses support.
Demonstrated reviewer competence, workable SOP/incident/fallback rehearsal and affected-user feedback can close their respective unknowns.
Verified demand, complete handling time, protected capacity, peaks and leave/support cover determine whether resources support the proposed volume.
A funded support/retirement plan and model/data/term changes require continuing review rather than a one-time readiness certificate.
Independent fit/value qualification and the Adoption Agent’s decision remain necessary before actual operating release.
Review requested planning evidence in two weeks or sooner after an approval, incident, owner or resource change; this is a proposed cadence, not a regulatory deadline.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Before any routine use, obtain a distinct operating route/approval, recurrent reviewer/support capacity, funded ownership, workflow/incident evidence and independent fit/value qualification.
Confirm L1 owner, cap, synthetic inputs and stopping criteria before actually starting learning.
